title: Holding a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan alongside Other Medicare Coverage
content:
A member enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan that includes prescription drug coverage may not also hold a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan, and Medicare will disenroll them from the Medicare Advantage plan if they try.

No Medicare Advantage enrollment that includes Part D coverage is in force for the same member on the day the stand-alone drug coverage would begin.

## What other coverage means for a stand-alone drug plan election

| What else the member holds | Whether a stand-alone Ridgecrest RxSecure election may stand alongside it |
| --- | --- |
| A Medicare Advantage plan that includes Part D drug coverage | no; the two may not be held together |
| A Medicare Advantage plan that carries no drug coverage | yes; the two are billed and appealed separately |
| A Medicare Supplement policy | yes; a supplement policy has carried no drug coverage for many years and never conflicts with a stand-alone drug plan |

## Where the conflicting plan is held

Where the member holds a Medicare Advantage plan that includes drug coverage the stand-alone election is not simply refused: the plan explains that accepting it would end their medical plan as well, and records the election only once the member says they understand.

## Where the member moves the other way

Where a member is moved out of this plan because they joined a Medicare Advantage plan with drug coverage, the disenrollment reason recorded is that they enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan with drug coverage, and coverage ends the day before the new plan begins.
